affected_system: walking, cycling, and shared micromobility network
alternatives: add targeted redundancy around the largest failure modes in active-mobility continuity under network and fleet disruption
select an adaptive robust portfolio across severe scenarios for active-mobility continuity under network and fleet disruption
pair link-failure, weather, and fleet-availability simulation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Trips, counts, facilities, stress levels, barriers, and shared-vehicle states use documented coverage.
Observed shared-system trips do not represent all walking and cycling demand.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: apply current continuity provisions to active-mobility continuity under network and fleet disruption.

constraints.description: The active mobility network and micromobility stress test must respect declared minimum continuity and safety thresholds across severe scenarios.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: active transportation director and shared-mobility program manager
decision_question: Which detours and operating plan preserve low-stress access during closures, weather, and fleet outages?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The active mobility network and micromobility stress test must respect declared minimum continuity and safety thresholds across severe scenarios.
independence_key.decision_object: active-mobility continuity under network and fleet disruption
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for active-mobility continuity under network and fleet disruption passes documented checks for scenario ranges, dependence, failure rates, recovery, intervention performance, and sensitivity.
independence_key.primary_outcome: essential trips without a low-stress feasible alternative

intended_claim: A versioned stress-test design for comparing declared alternatives affecting active-mobility continuity under network and fleet disruption, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: essential trips without a low-stress feasible alternative
distributional gap in essential trips without a low-stress feasible alternative
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not describe a modeled detour as field-verified safe or an assumed trip as observed.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for active-mobility continuity under network and fleet disruption passes documented checks for scenario ranges, dependence, failure rates, recovery, intervention performance, and sensitivity.

title: Stress-test active-mobility network continuity
